To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the US-induced hemolysis and the subsequent resealing in solution containing water-soluble protein can encapsulate concentrated protein into resealed erythrocyte ghost.

the addition of a small amount plasma and divalent ions to the solution containing water soluble proteins significantly increased the mean corpuscular concentration (MCC) of protein encapsulated in resealed erythrocyte by the US induced poration and reseal procedure.

a procedure of continuous-wave US-induced hemolysis and subsequent reseal in a solution containing water-soluble protein is applied to the encapsulation of concentrated protein into resealed rat red blood cell ghosts.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a novel method for encapsulation of protein solution with a high concentration.
a procedure of continuous-wave US-induced hemolysis and rescaling for encapsulation of concentrated protein solutions into erythrocytes.
the application of continuous-wave US for encapsulating protein solutions into reseal erythrocytes.

the present method is a promising technique for encapsulating concentrated water soluble protein solutions into erythrocytes.
this method is a useful tool for encapsulating concentrated water soluble protein solutions into reseal erythrocyte membranes.
the US-induced method of hemolysis and rescaling is an effective method of encapsulating concentrated protein solution into erythrocytes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the MCC is a function of the hemolysis and the resealing of the erythro- cyte membrane.
the MCC is determined by the balance between the degree of hemolytic damage and the efficiency of resealing.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the US-induced hemolysis method can encapsulate concentrated protein into erytrocyte porated with US.

the MCC of encapsulated protein can be significantly increased without any blood-washing procedure by the addition of a small amount (1%) of plasma and Ca(2+) (1mM) and Mg(2+)(0.1mM) into the resealing solution.

the continuous-wave US-induced hemolysis and subsequent reseal in the presence of plasma, Ca2+, and Mg2+ can provide a new method for the encapsulation of concentrated protein into resealed erythrocyte ghost, which may be useful as an alternative for protein encapsulation into liposomes.
